title: Molecular Dynamics Reveal Base Flipping as a Key Mechanism in Tc3a Transposase DNA Recognition
one_liner_zh: 该文通过分子动力学模拟揭示Tc3a转座酶N端乙酰化诱导碱基翻转的DNA识别机制，属于广义蛋白-DNA互作的结构动态研究，方法可迁移至TF-DNA体系，但对象非典型转录因子。
abstract: Transposons, or “jumping genes,” are mobile genetic elements that reshape genomes. The Tc1/Mariner family, including Tc3a transposase, has been studied for decades, but key aspects of its DNA recognition and cleavage remain unresolved. Existing models propose a homo-dimeric process for DNA excision and integration, yet conflicting hypotheses exist about the initial steps of DNA cleavage and target site recognition. Here, we reveal a previously unrecognized base-flipping mechanism in Tc3a transposase that challenges long-standing models of Mariner transposon activity. Using molecular dynamics simulations, we demonstrate that N-terminal acetylation induces a structural shift in the transposase-DNA complex, forcing a nucleotide in the inverted repeat to flip outward. This base-flipping event alters the local DNA conformation, creating torsional strain that may facilitate transposon inverted terminal repeat association. Unlike prior models, which assumed the entire protein, or protein dimers, were needed to illicit DNA interactions necessary for any types of torsion, our findings indicate that transposase bipartite binding itself actively reshapes DNA structure. We further show that this mechanism is dependent on the bipartite helix-turn-helix domains, which differentially contribute to DNA stabilization and recognition. Our simulations also reveal that the processed N-terminus plays an unexpected role in modulating DNA binding affinity, contradicting previous assumptions that it was structurally inconsequential. Together, the two helix-turn-helix motifs act to propagate the force caused by base flipping along one direction of the cognate DNA double helix axis. The fact that previous structural studies lacked this amino acid modification may explain why this mechanism was overlooked. These results provide a new framework for understanding transposase-DNA interactions, highlighting how a single molecular modification can trigger major DNA rearrangements. This discovery not only redefines the Tc3a transposition process but also calls for a reassessment of long-standing Mariner family transposon models.
abstract_zh: 转座子，或称“跳跃基因”，是可移动的遗传元件，能够重塑基因组。Tc1/Mariner家族，包括Tc3a转座酶，已被研究数十年，但其DNA识别和切割的关键方面仍未解决。现有模型提出DNA切除和整合涉及同源二聚体过程，然而关于DNA切割的初始步骤和靶位点识别存在相互矛盾的假说。在此，我们揭示了Tc3a转座酶中一种先前未被识别的碱基翻转机制，这挑战了Mariner转座子活性的长期模型。利用分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟，我们证明N端乙酰化诱导转座酶-DNA复合物发生结构转变，迫使反向重复序列中的一个核苷酸向外翻转。这一碱基翻转事件改变了局部DNA构象，产生扭转应力，可能促进转座子反向末端重复序列的关联。与先前模型不同——这些模型假设整个蛋白质或蛋白质二聚体是引发任何类型扭转所需DNA相互作用的前提——我们的发现表明，转座酶的双部分结合本身即主动重塑DNA结构。我们进一步显示，这一机制依赖于双部分螺旋-转角-螺旋结构域，这些结构域在DNA稳定化和识别中发挥差异化作用。我们的模拟还揭示，经加工的N端在调节DNA结合亲和力中扮演意外角色，这与先前认为其在结构上无关紧要的假设相矛盾。共同地，两个螺旋-转角-螺旋基序沿同源DNA双螺旋轴的一个方向传播由碱基翻转引起的力。先前结构研究缺乏这种氨基酸修饰的事实，可能解释了为何这一机制被忽视。这些结果为理解转座酶-DNA相互作用提供了新框架，突显了单一分子修饰如何触发重大DNA重排。这一发现不仅重新定义了Tc3a转座过程，还呼吁重新评估长期存在的Mariner家族转座子模型。
